sources.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Cambridge University Press (2018), author-hosted prepublication text
sources.locator: Ch. 2 §§2.1.2–2.2.2 for density operators, channels, Kraus and Stinespring representations; Ch. 5 §§5.2.1–5.2.3 (printed pp. 265–281) for von Neumann entropy, support-sensitive QRE, joint convexity and channel monotonicity; §5.3.3 (printed pp. 294–298) for cq states and the Holevo information.
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author-hosted 598-page book PDF. The book uses base-2 logarithms; local items explicitly convert to the repository's natural-log nats convention by the factor ln 2.

read_evidence.extent: The complete PDF was downloaded and text-extracted with MuPDF. The cited sections were inspected in full, including Watrous's complete proof of Theorem 5.35 via joint convexity, mixed-unitary monotonicity, and Stinespring dilation. The local item proofs use a separate resolvent and finite-twirl derivation.

contents.name: §5.2.1 definitions of von Neumann entropy and support-sensitive quantum relative entropy
contents.detail: The spectral formulas and support branch are used, with an explicit conversion from the book's bits to natural-log nats and a stated zero-eigenvalue convention.

contents.name: §5.2.3 joint convexity and monotonicity of quantum relative entropy
contents.detail: The theorem scope is retained. Its proof is supplied locally through inverse compression, the resolvent formula for negative logarithm, relative modular operators, regularization, a finite unitary twirl, and Kraus dilation; no cited theorem replaces the local proof.

contents.name: §5.3.3 classical-quantum state and Holevo information formulas
contents.detail: The finite ensemble and average-state formulas are adopted with zero-probability branches explicitly omitted.

contents.name: §5.3.3 accessible-information bound for measurements
contents.detail: The full measurement bound is locally proved from channel data processing and the finite POVM channel construction.

sources.title: Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, arXiv:1106.1445v8
sources.locator: Ch. 11 §§11.1 and 11.8–11.9 for finite quantum entropy, quantum relative entropy, mutual-information identities, conditional entropy, and the Holevo measurement-bound statement; Ch. 12 §12.5 for the full recoverability strengthening whose nonnegative remainder implies QRE data processing.
sources.source_kind_detail: Independent book-length graduate lecture notes, complete 774-page arXiv PDF.

read_evidence.extent: The complete PDF and text extraction were available in the prior information-theory research archive. The cited Ch. 11 sections and the complete Ch. 12 §12.5 proof were inspected. Wilde states the QRE data-processing theorem in §11.8, defers its proof to Ch. 12, and derives it there from a stronger fidelity/recovery inequality using complex interpolation; the local items provide an independent proof and make no recovery claim.

contents.name: §11.1 finite quantum entropy and mutual-information identities
contents.detail: The finite-dimensional scope and entropy identities are retained; the local definitions use the repository's linear-first convention.

contents.name: §11.8 quantum relative entropy and its data-processing theorem statement
contents.detail: The support inclusion condition and infinite-value branch are included; the local definition fixes natural logarithms.

contents.name: §11.9 Holevo measurement-bound exercise
contents.detail: The claim is included, while the exercise-only source route is replaced by a complete local proof.

contents.name: §11.7 negative conditional entropy for entangled states
contents.detail: The Bell-pair calculation makes the possible negativity explicit without asserting nonnegativity of quantum conditional entropy.

contents.name: §12.5 recovery maps and quantitative near-equality theorem
contents.reason: The assigned page requires finite-channel QRE data processing, not a recovery theorem or equality characterization. The full source proof was read; no recovery claim is imported.

pages.source_context: The examples page is the companion of the A page and uses the two independently read full-text treatments recorded above.

supported_examples.detail: The eigenvalue calculation and 0 log 0 endpoint convention are checked locally.
The mixture spectrum, branch entropies, and projective outcome law are calculated locally.
Orthogonal pure states witness the support-failure branch in the QRE definition.
Both reduced states and the joint entropy are computed from the partial-trace definition.
